problem: Indoor semantic region mapping (bedroom, kitchen, etc.) is usually done by detecting objects and inferring the room label. This fails when objects appear in multiple regions, regions are not clearly delineated, or regions contain few objects (e.g. hallway). Off-the-shelf scene classifiers trained on web photos transfer poorly to robot egocentric views.
motivation: Robots need high-level, explainable semantic understanding of large regions, which is under-explored compared with object labeling and scene graphs. Holistic image-level cues from a vision-language model can capture region identity without object recognition, but pretrained CLIP performs poorly on simulator indoor images, so it needs adaptation and grounding into a spatial map.
key_idea: Finetune CLIP with a multi-modal supervised contrastive loss for region classification, inject its spatial features into a learned RGB-D neural mapper that fuses egocentric region maps into a global region map during exploration.
insight: Holistic CLIP features beat object-based region inference: in online mapping the oracle object-detection baseline gets 26.58 maskAcc versus 40.81 for the ViT spatial-feature mapper. Naively projecting the CLIP class prediction into the map gives only about 4-5% accuracy offline, while injecting the features into a learned mapper reaches about 31%. Spatial features help only with ViT-B/32. A moving-average map update beats a Bayesian update (13.08 vs 40.81 maskAcc), because neural classifiers give spurious, rapidly flipping high-confidence predictions.
method: Offline dataset: 236K RGB-D/top-down region-map pairs (228K train, 8K val) collected in Habitat on Matterport3D by running the exploration policy of Bigazzi et al. (FOCUS); 14 filtered region labels, 224x224 observations, 101x101 maps.
Region classification module: CLIP (ResNet50 or ViT-B/32) with cosine similarity between image features and text features of the region labels; only the projection layers are finetuned.

Multi-modal supervised contrastive loss (MSCL): extends SupCon to image and text features; the image label is the majority region in the GT top-down map, unique label text embeddings are added to the batch, and all same-label items count as positives.

Egocentric region mapper: ResNet-18+UNet on RGB, UNet on the top-down depth point cloud, and CLIP multi-level features upsampled by transposed convolutions and merged. Two UNet decoders output an occupancy map (with inference of occluded areas) and a region map, masked to the visible area via depth.
Global map fusion: local maps are rotated and translated by the pose into a 2001x2001x(2+C) global map using a moving average (a Bayesian update is compared).
Navigation: hierarchical exploration policy (global goal on the map, deterministic planner, local policy) that takes the region-aware global map as input.

setting.backbone: CLIP ViT-B/32 (projection finetuned) + ResNet-18/UNet mapper + hierarchical exploration policy (trained)
setting.training_data: 236K observation-map pairs from Matterport3D (228K train / 8K val) collected via exploration in Habitat; CLIP pretrained on web image-text
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D 224x224 with pose (perfect, or Habitat noise models in one variant)
setting.action_space: low-level: forward 0.25 m, turn left 10°, turn right 10°; hierarchical global goal / local goal
setting.privileged: GT pose and depth assumed (noise variant tested); GT region maps used for training; oracle object detector only in a baseline

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark; results are on the authors' own region-mapping dataset/protocol.
results: The ViT-B/32 spatial-feature mapper reaches 40.81 maskAcc, 22.70 ovrAcc and 24.68 IoU online, beating an oracle object-detection baseline (26.58/8.63/19.44) and a Places365 scene-classifier baseline (28.46/9.42/21.03). With noisy pose and depth it still outperforms the noise-free baselines on maskAcc (32.73) and IoU (22.08), though not on ovrAcc (13.74 vs 9.42 is higher, so it also beats them there).
limitations: Absolute accuracy is low (about 31% offline pixel accuracy and 44.75% classification, near the 49.6% human level), with overfitting in finetuning.
Only 14 coarse labels on Matterport3D, the only dataset with room annotations; no real-robot experiments; assumes perfect pose and depth in the main results.
Downstream navigation benefits of the region map are not evaluated.
